world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: [p. 29] Cette difficulté est due au fait qu'en élicitation, les informateurs samayé ont tendance a accentuée [sic] la pénultième. La distinction entre l'accentuation et l'allongement vocalique n'étant pas encore de mes capacités, toutes les réalisations allongées n'ont pas été percues. [p. 55] La voyelle centrale [ə] n'est jamais en opposition avec [a] et sa distribution est limitée (finale non accentuée). [p. 62] Le samayé, comme la grande majorité des langues bantoues est une langue à tons.
new_statements.translation: [p. 29] This difficulty is due to the fact that, in elicitation, the Samayé informants tend to accent the penultimate. Since distinguishing accentuation from vowel lengthening is not yet within my abilities, not all lengthened realisations were perceived. [p. 55] The central vowel [ə] is never in opposition with [a] and its distribution is limited (unaccented final). [p. 62] Samayé, like the great majority of Bantu languages, is a tone language.
new_statements.citation: Mokrani, Soraya. 2005. Eléments nouveaux en vue de la description de la langue samayé (B25): éléments de phonologie et de morphologie. Mémoire de Master 2, Université Lumière Lyon 2. 150 pp.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Osamayi is a tone language with two contrastive tones (H, L; a phonetic mid arises from lowering/downstep) and no phonological stress. Prominence ('accent') falls on the penultimate syllable of words pronounced in isolation; the final syllable is unaccented (its /a/ reduces to [ə]; vowel timbre is hard to hear there), and the perceived vowel length on the penult is treated as an accentual effect rather than a length contrast.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the author frames penultimate accent as an elicitation-form tendency and admits she could not reliably separate accent from vowel length. The B-falling tone occurs only in absolute final position and only with one informant.
new_statements.domain_note: Words in isolation / elicitation citation forms (nouns and verbs from a c. 800-item wordlist); the penultimate lengthening 'disappears' in phrases (p. 55). No systematic stress section; the statement is incidental to the vowel-length discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Mokrani 2005 calls the language 'samayé' (= osamayi per Kwenzi-Mikala 1987, also 'shamayé'), Guthrie B25 / Maho B.203, spoken in the Ivindo basin (Mekambo) and at Okondja; principal informant from the village of Itebe (Sébé-Brikolo department, Haut-Ogooué), second informant Eugénie Zima. This is the same languoid as osam1235 (ISO syx); no dialect is distinguished.

sources.note: Tonal language (two distinctive tones /H/ and /B/, phonetic M by downstep/lowering, B-falling only utterance-finally; Ch. 4 pp. 62-74). No stress section, but incidental first-hand remarks: in elicitation the informants 'ont tendance a accentuée la pénultième' (p. 29); vowel length is judged accentual, not distinctive (p. 55); the final syllable is 'non accentuée', where /a/ reduces to [ə] (pp. 29, 55).
